html:
The Kenyan crisis began after the election of 27 December 2007, when President Mwai Kibaki was declared the winner over Raila Odinga amid wide claims of rigging, and lasted into early 2008.

Protests turned into ethnic violence, especially in the Rift Valley and the slums of Nairobi. Over a thousand people were killed and hundreds of thousands driven from their homes. In one attack, a church near Eldoret was burned with people inside.

Kofi Annan, the former head of the United Nations, mediated a deal in February 2008 that made Odinga prime minister in a coalition government. Reforms followed, above all the Constitution of 2010. Uhuru Kenyatta and William Ruto were later charged at the International Criminal Court, but the cases collapsed. It came after the long rule of Moi in Kenya.
sum: The Kenyan crisis began after the election of 27 December 2007, when President Mwai Kibaki was declared the winner over Raila Odinga amid wide claims of rigging, and lasted into early 2008.
